title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten admission-free ways to share art, science, green space, and public culture on campus and around Philadelphia.

cards.title: Compare Notes at Pearlstein
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art with free public admission
cards.notes: Walk through the current exhibition together, then trade observations before leaving.
cards.short_summary: An easy indoor meetup centered on Drexel’s contemporary exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pearlstein Gallery invites visitors to experience contemporary exhibitions without an admission charge.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public when exhibitions are on view. Check the gallery site for exhibition dates and seasonal closures.

cards.title: Browse the Founding Collection
cards.subtitle: A short weekday gallery meetup
cards.notes: Pick one work each to examine, then compare what caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: See part of the Drexel Founding Collection together without paying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Anthony J. Drexel Picture Gallery houses part of the Drexel Founding Collection and is open to the public without admission.
cards.access_notes: Public access is listed Monday–Friday, 3:30–5 p.m. The gallery closes on Sundays, major holidays, and during its stated winter break.

cards.title: Take a Rincliffe Art Break
cards.subtitle: Free public viewing on weekdays
cards.notes: Use the gallery as a compact group break and discuss the displayed Founding Collection works.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket art stop inside Drexel’s Main Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Rincliffe Gallery displays works from the Drexel Founding Collection with free public admission.
cards.access_notes: Public access is listed Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Holiday and winter-break closures apply.

cards.title: Catch a Free Portal Program
cards.subtitle: Public outdoor culture at 40th and Baltimore
cards.notes: Choose a listed free performance or community program and meet at the garden.
cards.short_summary: Recurring admission-free programming in a public outdoor space.
cards.evidence_claim: University City District programs free, family-friendly events at Trolley Portal Gardens, including recurring outdoor music performances.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor venue. Consult the official calendar for free-event dates and weather changes; food purchases are optional.

cards.title: See Contemporary Art at ICA
cards.subtitle: Always-free admission for everyone
cards.notes: Walk the exhibitions as a group and regroup afterward to discuss one work apiece.
cards.short_summary: A public contemporary-art outing near Drexel with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: ICA Philadelphia states that it is always free for all and presents contemporary art at 118 South 36th Street.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to everyone. Check the official site before visiting because galleries may close between exhibitions.

cards.title: Follow the History of Materials
cards.subtitle: Free public science galleries
cards.notes: Explore the permanent exhibitions together or try a self-guided puzzle or activity sheet.
cards.short_summary: A group museum visit built around science, objects, and materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science History Institute Museum is free and open to the public, with permanent exhibitions, interactive features, and self-guided activities.
cards.access_notes: Public access is Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., subject to listed holiday closures. Groups larger than 12 must reserve; visitors under 16 need a guardian.

cards.title: Walk and Swing at the Rail Park
cards.subtitle: A free elevated public-space meetup
cards.notes: Wander the paths, sit on the bench swings, and use the skyline as a conversation backdrop.
cards.short_summary: An admission-free outdoor hang with paths, seating, and city views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rail Park states that Phase One is free and open to the public daily, with paths, bench swings, and city views.
cards.access_notes: Public access is listed daily from 7 a.m.–10 p.m. The wheelchair-accessible entrance is on Noble Street just east of Broad Street.

cards.title: Walk the Woodlands Grounds
cards.subtitle: Historic green space open every day
cards.notes: Take a quiet group walk while respecting graves, funerals, and people visiting loved ones.
cards.short_summary: A daytime walk through a historic site and active cemetery in West Philadelphia.
cards.evidence_claim: The Woodlands identifies its grounds as a historic site, active cemetery, and large West Philadelphia green space open 365 days a year from dawn until dusk.
cards.access_notes: The grounds are publicly accessible from dawn until dusk. Follow site rules, yield to funerals, and leave promptly as the gates close near sunset. Paid guided tours are separate and unnecessary for this hang.

cards.title: Browse Parkway Central Together
cards.subtitle: Public collections, galleries, and Wi-Fi
cards.notes: Choose a department or gallery to explore together; borrowing is not required for an on-site browse.
cards.short_summary: A public-library meetup with books, exhibitions, seating, and browsing space.
cards.evidence_claim: Parkway Central Library welcomes visitors and lists shelf browsing, public computers, Wi-Fi, study rooms, and gallery departments among its services and facilities.
cards.source_title: Parkway Central Library — Free Library of Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted library hours. General on-site browsing requires no purchase; borrowing and some services may require a library card or reservation.

cards.title: Take a Bartram’s Garden Walk
cards.subtitle: Nearly 50 acres with free daily access
cards.notes: Walk the grounds, check what is blooming, and pause by the riverfront without booking a tour.
cards.short_summary: A free group walk through a public garden and riverfront park.
cards.evidence_claim: Bartram’s Garden describes itself as a nearly 50-acre public park whose grounds are free and open to everyone every day from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian access is free from sunrise to sunset. Programs, amenities, the welcome center, and the historic house follow separate schedules.

warnings: Free status covers the described admission-free activity only; optional transportation, food, merchandise, rentals, tours, and separately ticketed programming are not included.
Hours and exhibition schedules can change; use each linked official page before departure.
Coordinates are included only where supplied by the research dossier; no coordinates were inferred for newly researched subjects.
